title: Unit – 3 : Session – 1 : SLO – 1 | Introduction to Concurrent Programming
sections: Fill: In concurrent programming, multiple THREADS (tasks) can be executed in overlapping time periods.
T/F: A thread is a lightweight process used in concurrent programming. — TRUE
MCQ: Commonly used for managing concurrency → A) Semaphore
Fill: A DEADLOCK condition occurs when two or more threads wait for each other indefinitely.
T/F: Context switching allows a single processor to execute multiple threads by rapidly switching between them. — TRUE
MCQ: Mechanism used to protect shared data → A) Mutex
Fill: RACE CONDITION is the term when two threads access shared data at the same time, leading to unpredictable results.
T/F: Concurrent programming is only possible on multi-core processors. — FALSE (possible on a single core via context switching)
MCQ: Example of a synchronization mechanism → A) Condition variable
Fill: A MUTEX (lock) ensures that only one thread accesses a critical section at a time.
